findings.issue: Falsy evaluation of limit bypasses filtering when max_price is zero
findings.evidence: Implement filter(items, limit): if limit: return [p for p in items if p.price_cents <= limit]; otherwise return items.
findings.failure_scenario: When a client passes max_price=0 to request only free products (R1), limit evaluates to false (0 is falsy), returning all catalog items instead of only items with price_cents <= 0.
findings.fix: Check explicitly whether limit is not None (e.g., 'if limit is not None:') before applying the filter.

findings.issue: Pagination is executed before filtering instead of filtering before pagination
findings.evidence: page=paginate(rows, offset, size); return filter(page, max_price) vs R2: 'Filter the entire tenant's catalog, sort by immutable product ID ascending, THEN paginate.'
findings.failure_scenario: Paginating before filtering causes pages to be under-filled or empty whenever expensive products occupy the page window, even if matching affordable products exist in later slices of the catalog.
findings.fix: Filter rows by max_price first, sort by immutable product ID, and then paginate the filtered collection.

findings.issue: Test suite omits boundary limit=0 and multi-page pagination test cases
findings.evidence: test missing limit, limit=1500, negative, decimal and tenant isolation. Test data has two matching products and two expensive ones, all within a single page.
findings.failure_scenario: Tests will pass as false positives despite T1 failing on limit=0 and T2 paginating before filtering, because limit=0 is not asserted and all test items reside on a single page.
findings.fix: Add test cases for limit=0 asserting only zero-price items return, and add test fixtures spanning multiple pages to verify pagination occurs after filtering.
